comment: Identity, consent, time, authentication, provenance, audit, authorisation and accountability are addressed across the draft, but they are dispersed across principles and component requirements rather than declared as architecture-wide protected invariants. During mapping, transformation, aggregation, exchange or AI reuse, these properties may be weakened or stripped even when the transaction remains technically valid.

public.text: Identity, consent, time, authentication, provenance, audit, authorisation and accountability are addressed across the draft, but they are dispersed across principles and component requirements rather than declared as architecture-wide protected invariants. During mapping, transformation, aggregation, exchange or AI reuse, these properties may be weakened or stripped even when the transaction remains technically valid.
public.suggestedRevision: Define a small set of protected architecture-wide invariants that every DPI-H component, interface and transformation must preserve or explicitly and lawfully supersede which are identity and identity-resolution status; consent/permission; event time; source and authorship; provenance and lineage; authorisation/verification status; audit history; and accountable ownership. Require conformance and regression tests to detect alteration, loss or ambiguity of these invariants.
